Transformer FAQ

Cast resin vs VPI dry-type transformer: what is the difference?

Cast resin embeds the winding in a solid resin body, while VPI impregnates the winding insulation with varnish under vacuum and pressure.

Engineering guidanceLast reviewed: July 2026

Direct answer

Cast resin construction provides a solid encapsulated winding with strong resistance to moisture and contamination. VPI construction uses vacuum-pressure impregnation to fill winding voids with insulating varnish while retaining a more open winding structure. Neither system is universally superior; the selection depends on environment, thermal duty, mechanical requirements, repair strategy, standards and cost.

Article contentsCast resin characteristicsVPI characteristicsHow to chooseRelated termsProject review

Cast resin characteristics

Cast resin windings can provide strong environmental protection and low partial-discharge performance when correctly manufactured. Thermal expansion, resin formulation and quality control are important.

VPI characteristics

VPI windings generally offer good heat transfer and avoid a thick rigid casting. Environmental protection may rely more heavily on insulation system quality and enclosure design.

How to choose

Compare humidity and contamination, thermal cycling, overload duty, partial-discharge requirement, enclosure, repairability, certification and local market practice.
